summary: Chinese frames time with words AFTER the time phrase, and the whole phrase stands before the verb: 八点以前 ‘before eight’, 吃饭以后 ‘after eating’, 假期期间 ‘during the holidays’, 吃饭的时候 ‘while eating’, 从去年以来 ‘since last year’. ‘Until’ is 到 (after a verb: 工作到六点) or 直到 (直到十二点才回家 ‘not until twelve’); ‘since’ is 自从 … (以后 / 以来) or 从 … 以来; ‘from … to …’ is 从 … 到 …. ‘At / on / in’ a time has NO word at all: 我七点吃早饭 ‘at seven’, 星期一 ‘on Monday’, 五月 ‘in May’, 冬天 ‘in winter’ (formal writing may add 在). The clock: number + 点 (o’clock) + number + 分 (minutes), 半 for half past: 八点半, 下午三点十分. The date goes from big to small: 年 → 月 → 号 (spoken) / 日 (written): 2026年五月一号. Months are numbered: 一月 … 十二月; 三月 ‘March’ but 三个月 ‘three months’.

blocks.title: Postpositions of time — like the place words of S12
blocks.text: 桌子上 ‘on the table’ put the place word after the noun (S12); time works the same way: 八点以前, 吃饭以后, 假期期间. 以前 / 以后 even use the words for ‘front’ and ‘back’ (前面, 后面).

blocks.title: No ‘at / on / in’
blocks.text: Greek στις πέντε, German um fünf, am Montag, im Mai — Chinese: 五点, 星期一, 五月, just before the verb: 我五点走. (Greek τη Δευτέρα and German heute also do without a preposition — Chinese does so everywhere.)

items.title: 三月 — March
points: 我三月去。 I’m going in March.

items.title: 三个月 — three months
points: 我去三个月。 I’m going for three months.

blocks.title: Where a length of time goes
blocks.text: WHEN comes before the verb (我八点工作 ‘I work at eight’); HOW LONG comes after it (我工作八个小时 ‘I work for eight hours’).

items.title: 到 — until (everyday)
points: 我们等到明天吧。 Let’s wait until tomorrow.
从早到晚 from morning till night

items.title: 直到 … 才 … — not until
points: 他直到十二点才回家。 He didn’t come home until twelve.

blocks.title: Asking
blocks.text: 现在几点？ · 今天几号？ · 你的生日是几月几号？ · 你什么时候走？— 吃饭以后。

askYourself: Is it simply WHEN (at, on, in)? → the time word alone, before the verb: 七点, 星期一, 五月.
Before / after a time or an event? → time + 以前 / 之前, event + 以后 / 之后 — the word comes after.
Until? → verb + 到 + time (工作到六点); ‘not until’ → 直到 … 才 ….
Since (up to now)? → 从 … 以来 / 自从 … (以后).
During? → noun + 期间 / 里; a clause + 的时候.
From … to …? → 从 A 到 B.
Is it HOW LONG, not when? → after the verb (工作八个小时).
A clock time? → 点 + 分 / 半; 2 o’clock = 两点. A date? → 年 → 月 → 号, big to small.
steps: Build the time phrase (time + 以前 / 以后 / 期间 …).
Put it before the verb (at the start or after the subject).
Then the verb and the rest.

traps: *我工作八点 (for ‘at eight’) → 我八点工作; 我工作八个小时 = ‘for eight hours’.
*他直到十二点不回家 → 他直到十二点才回家.
*自从明天 → 从明天起 (自从 only for the past).

quiz.why: No word for ‘at’; the time stands before the verb.
Month before day: big to small.
三月 is March; a count needs 个.
‘Not until’ = 直到 … 才 …, without 不.
以后 follows the event; 以前 means ‘before’.
How long goes after the verb; 我八点工作 is ‘I work at eight’.

seeAlso.note: German puts the preposition first and chooses the case: vor / nach dem Essen (dative), bis acht, seit einem Jahr (dative, with the present tense), während der Ferien (genitive), um acht, am Montag, im Mai; Chinese has postpositions (吃饭以前, 假期期间), no case, and nothing for um / am / im.
Arabic uses قَبْلَ and بَعْدَ (+ genitive), حَتَّى ‘until’, مُنْذُ ‘since’, خِلَالَ ‘during’ and فِي السَّاعَةِ الْخَامِسَةِ ‘at five’ — all before the noun; Chinese reverses the order: 吃饭以前, 五点.
Hebrew לִפְנֵי / אַחֲרֵי, עַד, מֵאָז, בְּמֶשֶׁךְ and בְּשָׁעָה חָמֵשׁ come before the time; לִפְנֵי is also ‘in front of’, just as 以前 shares 前 with 前面.
The same rule as S14: the time phrase stands before the verb.
